heroLead: New Alexandria sits along the Loyalhanna Creek in Westmoreland County, farm and small-town ground that's seen its share of Marcellus and deeper Utica interest over the past fifteen years.
intro: A lot of the land around New Alexandria has stayed in agricultural use even as leasing activity picked up, and that combination, working farms with active gas units underneath, describes a lot of the mineral interests we come across in this part of Westmoreland County.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around New Alexandria directly. We review your title and production history carefully and explain exactly what we find.

sections.heading: Loyalhanna Valley Development
paragraphs: Westmoreland County's mix of Marcellus and deeper Utica potential has kept operator interest steady around New Alexandria over the years, even through periods when gas prices slowed drilling elsewhere. If your family's tract has been part of a unit since the early years, expect the production numbers to reflect a well that's moved past its initial peak.
This area sits in the wet-gas window, so liquids revenue and the associated processing deductions are both part of understanding your net royalty.

sections.heading: Working Through Westmoreland County Deed Records
paragraphs: We trace your chain of title through the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg, checking for older reservations or conveyances that might affect what your family currently holds.
Rural tracts around New Alexandria sometimes carry deed language referencing old farm boundaries, which we reconcile against current parcel and unit maps as part of our review.

sections.heading: A Clear Explanation Before Any Number
paragraphs: Before discussing an offer, we'll walk through your division order and royalty history so you understand your decimal interest and what's shaping its current value.

faqs.question: Does farming continue on land with active gas units nearby?
faqs.answer: Yes, surface farming and underground gas production commonly coexist, since horizontal wells are typically produced from pads sited away from actively farmed fields.

faqs.question: Is my interest affected by the Utica shale being deeper than the Marcellus?
faqs.answer: Your interest generally covers all oil and gas formations under your parcel unless your deed specifically limits it, so both Marcellus and deeper Utica rights are usually part of the same evaluation.

faqs.question: What if my deed references old farm boundary markers?
faqs.answer: That's common in this part of Westmoreland County, and we're experienced reconciling that language against current records during title research.

faqs.question: Is my interest still worth reviewing if drilling near New Alexandria has slowed recently?
faqs.answer: Yes. A well past its early peak can still carry real value, and we evaluate based on actual trailing production rather than the pace of new drilling nearby.

faqs.question: How long does your review typically take?
faqs.answer: Most reviews take one to two weeks once we have your deed and any lease or royalty paperwork you can share, and we'll keep you updated along the way.
